speaker: Head Coach
quote_text:
Get through this one quick then. Vinny. Arne,  congratulations. Finally the first time of  
asking. How did it feel? Pleasant. Although if  you know me a little bit, my thoughts are more  
on Sunday already than thinking about a final in  a month. But our performance today was something  
that pleased me most. Reaching a final should  always be special, even for this club. because  
this club is used to playing finals, but still  then we are working very hard every single day  
to try to improve players and the players want  to improve themselves every single day. But we're  
also in this business to play finals, although  we already know how difficult the final is going  
to be because we faced Newcastle already and they  were very impressive yesterday as well. But many  
games to be played before that final and this is  where our focus should be at. Just how impressive,  
though, were your players this evening, given  the control of where you went about in trailing  
for the first half? Yeah, very impressive. So  I think I'm not saying anything strange that  
Tottenham is conceding goals because they have  so many injury problems. That's probably the  
main reason why they are conceding goals, but they  are always able to score goals as well and create  
a lot And for us to be so aggressive without  the ball that it took them 80 minutes before  
they had their first shot on target, doesn't  tell you anything about Tottenham. That should  
tell you a lot about how we're great without the  ball. And I think that's what stood out for me,  
to play against a team that is so good in creating  chances, not conceding hardly. Only one shot is is  
is is in the end a good accomplishment. There  was a moment after Kohli scored the first goal  
and played to celebrate and Virgil very quickly  was sort of urging them to get back to the centre  
circle. How important is that mentality and that  relentlessness as well as obviously obviously that  
he got to how successful you are? Yeah, I saw the  same thing. I think there was a moment where you  
could see how we played for the whole game. It  was so intense. The players were ready for it,  
the fans were ready for it. And we all simply  wanted one thing and that's going through to  
the final. And that mentality we showed from the  first till the last second, but it was probably  
well shown in that moment as well. What honestly  did you think of the League Cup when you came in,  
say, the second domestic cup competition? Two  legend semi-final, it's more game and current  
season. Did some of you read or some of you could  have done that? No, no, definitely not going to go  
gone without. It has been most of the times games  where players that haven't played that much played  
a lot of minutes, and I think that has been  important for us as well, because every time we  
need one of these players, they are ready to play  as well. And I think if you come to this country,  
you know the history of the FA Cup and the League  Cup. I know as well, I think I say the correct  
thing, that the FA Cup is a bit higher than the  League Cup. But still, it's a cup and a trophy  
to win. And it is the one we won last season. And  I think if you win a trophy in the season before,  
you always have to take the challenge on trying to  win it again. Just a word on Cody Gap. Obviously,  
you get a lot of questions about Mo and his  numbers of goals. Cody's up to 15 now this  
season. I mean, firstly, how well is he playing,  but also, you know, can he get 25, something like  
that? I have no clue. I'm not so much into how  much goals they score. I know if they work as  
hard as they do and they bring the ball out of the  back as well as they do. then we will always score  
goals because of the quality players we have. But  these goals don't come from itself. If you look  
at the third goal, the effort Connor Bradley puts  in as a fullback to sprint all over the pitch and  
then assist towards Dom. That is just as important  as the one that scores goals. And I think it was  
Curtis who When I think it was Mo who crossed it  in, who went for it and that's why their fullback  
got a little bit of doubt and the ball falls down  to Cody. And if it's Cody or Lucio or Diogo or  
Darwin or Mo or Federico, they can all score  goals, but we have to make sure they come in those  
positions a lot. Therefore you need to run a lot  and that's what they are all doing. But Cody has  
a special season, but second-half of last season  he was special during the Euro He was special for  
Holland, so it doesn't doesn't come falling out  of the sky. Instead of English, it's it's it's  
something he did before. Chris, stronger and  better. For me, there are two reasons why we  
become stronger. One of one of first of all, if  you play more often together, you know better  
what is expected. So the first time I tell them  how to bring the ball out from the back against  
the 7-9-11 press, they were maybe like, okay, this  should be done. But the more times you face them,  
the more it just becomes natural for you. So that  helps. So the more games you play, the more team  
meetings you have, the more training sessions  you have, the better they know what we expect  
from them and what they have to expect from each  other. Second of all, I believe in the fact that  
the more games you play, the stronger you become,  the physically stronger you become. So some people  
think you get tired, but as long as you manage it  well, I think players will get stronger by playing  
a lot of games instead of getting tired. Hold on.  See you in the morning. Yeah, see you tomorrow.
title: Arne Slot post-match press conference | Liverpool 4-0 Tottenham (Agg 4-1)
